b: In the evening we went back to the airport to catch the next flight..Now we had to go to a place called Da Nang. Since I joined at the last minute, I still didn't know where each place was or what we were going to see..I just went along thinking if I go with them they'll show me something.
At the airport I bought Lay's chips and Milo.. Very cheap, and a different kind of taste.. This flight was better than the one we came on. They gave us water… but we fell asleep

By the time we arrived it was night…we went straight to the hotel.. They'd said there would be a swimming pool and all.. When we went and looked, our Wellawatte sea was better.. Looked like it hadn't been cleaned in years..

As soon as we got there we went out to eat at the shop opposite..Here I can tell you my tragedy.. In Vietnam there's no shortage of meat food.. Beef, mutton, chicken, pork, everything… and very tasty, it seems.. Everyone ate it happily.. I'm vegetarian.. They said there'd be food for me too… but since I grew up on pittu, dosai, rice and curry, I'm not used to eating raw leaves and greens.. Pizza and all was expensive.. But here, all they give you as vegetarian is boiled leaves and vegetables.. My mouth refused to let it down.Seeing this, my friends teased me as a fake vegetarian.. (Mithu said if I didn't mention this, she'd put my photo on posters all over town… I'm not scared, but just in case lots of people come looking for me after seeing my photo, I'll write it)
So mostly I had to quiet my hunger with chips, chocolate and biscuits.. Later, when they got sick of the food too, we found Indian shops and started eating there… only then did my soul find peace…

As soon as we'd eaten they said we had to go to the Dragon Bridge.. On Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights at 9 there's a show at the bridge… lots of people crowd in to see it… we got there just about in time

It's a big bridge like our Kelani bridge.. Built across the river.. Along the middle there was a dragon, long like a snake.. Its body curving up and down… its mouth facing the sky … People stood looking at its mouth.. At exactly nine it breathed fire three times… with coloured lights and fireworks, it was very beautiful… Perhaps because breathing fire burned its mouth, it then sprayed water from its mouth three times… Everyone standing close got soaked… We stood far away… We dreamed, like the curd-seller woman, that if we went back to Colombo and built lions and elephants on four or five bridges and made them breathe fire like this, people would come to see it. It would bring in good money

Then we went round that river looking at the shops and taking photos.. At one place they all sat cross-legged on the ground.. Since I'm the decent one among them, I didn't sit.. With the local people giving them funny looks as they passed, they got up and started walking…Since it was near the hotel we walked along chatting.. All useless chatter .. nothing much worth telling.. Talking, we walked a long way in the wrong direction.. Before walking back to the room we sat down at a juice shop

A street stall like our orange shops.. There too we had a good chat sitting on chairs by the road.. We thought we'd stay until the shopkeeper told us to go… he didn't.. That's how it is there.. People at every shop are nice… they don't tell you to go.. They only close up after we leave.. When we'd finished chatting like this and went to the room, it was one o'clock… as soon as we got there everyone went to bed
The next day we set off to look around an important place
note: The Kelani bridge crosses the Kelani river on the edge of Colombo. The curd-seller is the woman in the old fable who counts her riches before she has sold her curd. Pittu and dosai are everyday Jaffna dishes.
